title.narrative: West Bengal Drinking Water Sector Improvement Project

description.narrative: The project will provide safe and sustainable drinking water as per the standards set by the Government of India to about 1.65 million people in the arsenic, fluoride, and salinity- affected selected areas of Bankura, North 24 Parganas and Purba Medinipur districts of West Bengal (project districts). It will introduce an innovative and sustainable institutional framework and advanced technology for smart water management to enable efficient service delivery in project districts.

description.narrative: Output/s as listed by the project staff.

Output: Climate-resilient drinking water infrastructure constructed Indicator: 100% of water treatment plants, storage reservoirs, and distribution network commissioned under the project incorporate climate resilience measures (2017 baseline: Not applicable) Progress/Status: 79 storage reservoirs (of 37,350 kilo liters capacity) constructed. Work in progress for WTPs and the remaining storage reservoirs Data Source: PMU's annual reports, project quarterly progress reports Actual value:

Output: Climate-resilient drinking water infrastructure constructed Indicator: At least 7,200 kilometers of additional water distribution network laid and commissioned (2017 baseline: 0) Progress/Status: Total 6,474 km of additional pipelines laid in project districts. commissioning in progress in North 24 Parganas and Bankura. Data Source: PMU's annual reports, project quarterly progress reports Actual value:

Output: Climate-resilient drinking water infrastructure constructed Indicator: Connections to at least 390,000 households (100% of poor households and households headed by women) for 70 liters per capita per day of piped water supply and at least 8,000 government offices, educational institutions, commercial establishments, health centers completed Progress/Status: About 162,908 physical household connections completed against the target of 390,000. Data Source: PMU's annual reports, project quarterly progress reports Actual value:

Output: Climate-resilient drinking water infrastructure constructed Indicator: Four additional water treatment plants of 286 million liters per day of total capacity, and 126 storage reservoirs (ground level and overhead) with 99 million liters of total capacity commissioned, all equipped with smart water management devices (2017 baseline: 0) Progress/Status: water treatment plants with capacity of 287 million liters per day under construction with 2 at completion stage (being commissioned), and 135 storage reservoirs with total capacity of 83,700 kilo liters under construction with 88 reservoirs of total capacity of 41 MLD were commissioned. There are 10 packages under this project. The physical progress status on the packages is as folwooing: N24P-01 - 85% N24P-02A - 91% N24P-02B - 88% BKP-01 - 48% BK-02A - 79% BK-02B - 79% BK-03 - 98% BK-04 - 79% EM-01 - 71% Data Source: PMU's annual reports, project quarterly progress reports Actual value:

Output: Institutions and capacity of stakeholders for drinking water service delivery strengthened Indicator: At least 300 locals in project gram panchayats, with a minimum of 33% females, reported increased leadership and water-related livelihood skills (2017 baseline: 0, 0%) (OP 2.3.1, OP 6.1) Progress/Status: Training module preparation is ongoing. NGOs have substantially completed poverty mapping and identification of female and male candidates for leadership and skills training. Data Source: Annual reports, project quarterly progress reports from PMU and PHED Actual value:

Output: Institutions and capacity of stakeholders for drinking water service delivery strengthened Indicator: At least 500 locals in project gram panchayats, with a minimum of 33% females, reported increased awareness on water conservation, demand management, and water sanitation and hygiene (2017 baseline: 0, 0%) (OP 2.2) Progress/Status: Implementation of awareness campaigns started in all 3 districts by project NGOs. Targets are being regularly reported and tracked. (i) More than 40% female participation reported in awareness campaigns conducted so far. Data Source: Annual reports, project quarterly progress reports from PMU and PHED Actual value:

Output: Institutions and capacity of stakeholders for drinking water service delivery strengthened Indicator: At least 660 additional locals in project gram panchayats, with a minimum of 33% females, and a minimum of 200 PHED staff reported increased skills in utility management (2017 baseline: 0, 0%, 0) (OP 2.2, OP 6.1.1) Progress/Status: Preparation of training programs is going on in collaboration with SPM-NIWAS Data Source: Annual reports, project quarterly progress reports from PMU and PHED Actual value:

Output: Institutions and capacity of stakeholders for drinking water service delivery strengthened Indicator: Government order on AMSDF adopted by at least 70% of the project gram panchayats (2017 baseline: Not applicable) (OP 6.1) Progress/Status: GOWB issued the asset management and service delivery framework (AMSDF) that (i) defined the roles and responsibilities of the PHED, gram panchayats, panchayat samitis (governing bodies at block level), and zilla parishads (governing bodies at the district level); and (ii) set guidelines for operational sustainability parameters such as metering, tariff, and human resourcing.
Resolution from all 66 GPs for implementation of AMSDF has been obtained and process for ensuring adoption by the project team panchayats is under progress. Data Source: Annual reports, project quarterly progress reports from PMU and PHED
Actual value:

Output: Climate-resilient drinking water infrastructure constructed Indicator: Two pre-sedimentation tanks of 45 million liters capacity constructed and 3 tubewells of 2 million liters per day pumping capacity installed (2024 baseline: Not applicable) Data Source: PMU's annual reports, project quarterly progress reports Actual value:

Output: Institutions and capacity of stakeholders for drinking water service delivery strengthened Indicator: One operational plan to implement the AMSDF for project gram panchayats prepared (2024 baseline: 0) (OP 6.1) Data Source: Annual reports, project quarterly progress reports from PMU and PHED Actual value:

Output: Institutions and capacity of stakeholders for drinking water service delivery strengthened Indicator: One sustainable drinking water supply project proposal for salinity-affected areas of South 24 Parganas and unserved areas of Purba Medinipur districts prepared (2024 baseline: 0) (OP 3.2) Achievement: 1 Data Source: Annual reports, project quarterly progress reports from PMU and PHED

Output: Institutions and capacity of stakeholders for drinking water service delivery strengthened Indicator: District-level drinking water quality action plan developed for all districts of West Bengal (2017 baseline: 3 out of 23 districts) (OP 5.1) Progress/Status: District-wise DWQAP developed. (awaiting PMU submission of supporting documents). Data Source: Annual reports, project quarterly progress reports from PMU and PHED
Actual value:

Output: Institutions and capacity of stakeholders for drinking water service delivery strengthened Indicator: FSSM regulatory framework completed for West Bengal, and a pilot treatment plant commissioned in one project district (2017 baseline: not completed, not commissioned) (OP 3.2.5, OP 5.1.1) Progress/Status: The fecal sludge and septage management framework are completed for West Bengal by the government. Data Source: Annual reports, project quarterly progress reports from PMU and PHED Baseline year: 2017 Baseline value: not commissioned Baseline year: 2017 Baseline value: not commissioned Target year: 2027 Target value: commissioned

Output: Institutions and capacity of stakeholders for drinking water service delivery strengthened Indicator: Flood forecasting and early warning commissioned in Purba Medinipur (2017 baseline: Not commissioned) (3.2.2) Progress/Status: The flood forecasting and early warning was commissioned in Purba Medinipur. Data Source: Annual reports, project quarterly progress reports from PMU and PHED Baseline year: 2017 Baseline value: Not commissioned Baseline year: 2017 Baseline value: Not commissioned Target year: 2027 Target value: not commissioned

Output: Institutions and capacity of stakeholders for drinking water service delivery strengthened Indicator: Gender strategy for PHED developed (2017 baseline: Not applicable) (OP 2.3.2) Progress/Status: Selection of Individual Consultant is completed. Contract signing is in progress. Data Source: Annual reports, project quarterly progress reports from PMU and PHED Baseline year: 2017 Baseline value: Not applicable Baseline year: 2017 Baseline value: Not applicable Target year: 2027 Target value: developed

Output: Institutions and capacity of stakeholders for drinking water service delivery strengthened Indicator: Guidelines for water safety plan and sanitation safety plan for West Bengal developed (2017 baseline: Not completed) (OP 6.1) Progress/Status: Water Safety Plan for districts of N24P and Bankura developed and approved. Data Source: Annual reports, project quarterly progress reports from PMU and PHED Baseline year: 2017 Baseline value: Not completed Baseline year: 2017 Baseline value: Not completed Target year: 2027 Target value: developed

Output: Institutions and capacity of stakeholders for drinking water service delivery strengthened Indicator: Smart water management system commissioned in PHED and project gram panchayats. (2017 baseline: Not commissioned) (OP 6.1) Progress/Status: Smart water management application has been rolled out in three sample GPs and scaling up demonstrated in 6 GPs. Procurement for expansion to all project GPs is ongoing using grant 9196. Data Source: Annual reports, project quarterly progress reports from PMU and PHED Baseline year: 2017 Baseline value: commissioned Baseline year: 2017 Baseline value: commissioned Target year: 2027 Target value: not commissioned
Safe, sustainable, and inclusive drinking water service received in project districts.

At least 0.95 million people (0.30 million people from households headed by women and vulnerable households) receive potable bulk water supply in non-project gram panchayats in project districts (2017 baseline: No potable bulk water supply in non-project gram panchayats in project districts) Progress/Status: All contracts have been awarded. Households (HHs) survey in Bankura has been completed. HHs survey in N24P and East Medinipur substantially completed. Construction ongoing in all works packages. Data Source: Annual reports, including water quality, from PMU, PHED; and project quarterly progress reports Actual value:

At least 70% of project gram panchayats (governing bodies working at the village level) recover a minimum of 80% operation and maintenance costs, and operated with less than 15% nonrevenue water on average (2017 baseline: No services existed in project areas) Progress/Status: The GOWB issued the asset management and service delivery framework (AMSDF) that (i) defined the roles and responsibilities of the PHED, gram panchayats, panchayat samitis (governing bodies at block level), and zilla parishads (governing bodies at the district level); and (ii) set guidelines for operational sustainability parameters such as metering, tariff, and human resourcing. Data Source: Annual reports, including water quality, from PMU, PHED; and project quarterly progress reports Actual value:

At least 70% of project gram panchayats provide potable water supply on average to 100% of poor households and households headed by women, and operate services with a minimum of 33% female staff (2017 baseline: Not applicable) Progress/Status: Poverty and ethnicity mapping at village level undertaken using secondary data, for identification of FHH and vulnerable households and maintained in a roster at PIUs and GPs. Data Source: Annual reports, including water quality, from PMU, PHED; and project quarterly progress reports Actual value:

At least 1.65 million people (0.64 million people from households headed by women and vulnerable households)c receive continuous potable piped water supply (2017 baseline: 0.8 million people in project areas affected with arsenic, fluoride, and salinity; no piped water supply) Progress/Status: All contracts have been awarded. Households (HHs) survey in Bankura has been completed. HHs survey in N24P and East Medinipur substantially completed. Construction ongoing in all works packages. Data Source: Annual reports, including water quality, from PMU, PHED; and project quarterly progress reports Actual value:
